We are going to continue our aggressive pace for the remainder of this year because when Democrats take control of the Senate next year, our job is going to get a lot harder.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (Executive Session)
statements.title: Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (Executive Session)
sentences: These delays all add costs, and those costs are ultimately paid by families through things like higher energy costs, higher gas and diesel prices, and higher taxes.
We have talked about what this bill would do for energy projects, but there is another kind of project on a lot of Americans' minds right now, and that is data center construction.

Communities in my State of South Dakota and around our country are concerned about the movement of data centers into their communities, in particular, about what their construction could mean for energy prices.

For starters, it would require that the data centers shoulder the energy costs associated with their operation and construction, whether that is day-to-day running costs or the cost of additional infrastructure.

It also provides technical assistance to communities to help them understand and explore the impact a proposed data center would have on their locality--everything from the economic impact to the energy costs and infrastructure requirements that would be associated with the project.

And I am very pleased that this bill will extend Clean Water Act permits for farmers from 5 to 10 years, significantly reducing the frequency with which farmers have to engage with government bureaucracy with that process.

Well, I will tell you, because DC Water had first identified weaknesses in the pipe and proposed repairs a full 7 years earlier--7 years earlier--but had been prevented from starting that by a Federal permitting process that dragged on and on and on until the pipe suffered a catastrophic failure.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: I am proud of what Republicans have been able to accomplish for the American people in the 119th Congress--most especially, the Working Families Tax Cuts, which allows hard-working Americans to keep more of their hard-earned money.

As I said, I am proud that this Republican Congress has put more money in Americans' pockets with the Working Families Tax Cuts, and I am proud, too, of other measures we passed, like the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which will help address the cost of housing by increasing supply.
It does not mean standing by while Democrats attempt to reinstate the chaos that existed at the border under the Biden administration.
And so while Republicans are prepared to work in a bipartisan way, we will also emphatically oppose Democrats when required to protect hard- working Americans and our system of government.
We will oppose any attempt to balloon the size of the government or tear down American institutions, as the Democratic Socialists would like to do.
So we will see what the 120th Congress brings.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: BUSINESS BEFORE THE SENATE
statements.title: BUSINESS BEFORE THE SENATE
sentences: Today, we will be voting on two eminently commonsense pieces of legislation: the Stop Insider Trading Act and the Ratepayer Protection Act.
The Stop Insider Trading Act actually pairs two commonsense measures: a stock purchase ban for Members of Congress and a voter ID measure.

To ensure that Members of Congress and their families are not benefiting financially from insider knowledge of the market, the stock purchase ban would prohibit Members of Congress, their spouses, or their dependent children from purchasing stocks issued by public companies while the Member is in office.
The other half of the Stop Insider Trading Act is also pretty simple.
It would do nothing more than require that Americans present a photo ID when they go to vote.

While this vote should be a no-brainer, I do have some concerns, because while the American people overwhelmingly support a photo ID requirement, for some bizarre reason, congressional Democrats have decided that photo ID for voting is a step too far.
I say ``bizarre'' because I haven't seen Democrats crusading against showing ID in any of the other situations where Americans are required to present their photo identification.
My Democrat colleagues don't seem to have a problem with showing photo ID to board an airplane, to rent a car, to start a new job.
They don't seem to have a problem with showing photo ID at the doctor's office or when buying alcohol or when opening a bank account.
They don't seem to have a problem--if the Presiding Officer can believe this, they don't seem to have a problem with having a requirement to show a photo ID at their own political events.

It is only when it comes to voting that congressional Democrats suddenly, inexplicably see photo ID as a terrible problem, even though not only the majority of Americans but the majority of Democrats support photo identification.

I will say that 13 House Democrats found voter ID and the stock purchase ban to be so common sense that they broke with their party and supported the Stop Insider Trading Act when it moved through the House.
In addition to the Stop Insider Trading Act, the Senate will be voting on the Ratepayer Protection Act this week as well.
It would simply promote the adoption of a standard that would require data centers to shoulder the electricity costs associated with their operation and construction.
That is it--a simple piece of legislation designed to protect hard-working Americans from the increased energy costs associated with data centers.
Will Democrats support commonsense measures like a stock purchase ban, photo ID to vote, and protection from higher energy costs?
I guess we will see soon enough.
But they have another chance this week, and I guess we will see.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: As these entrepreneurs get underway, their businesses will be able to take advantage of the pro-growth tax reform the Republicans enacted last year in the Working Families Tax Cuts.

An agricultural co-op in my State says the 199A small business deduction, which Republicans first implemented with the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act back in 2017, has allowed them to pass $140 million in tax savings back to South Dakota farmers over the last decade.

Just to the west, a rancher in Montana said, thanks to the Working Families Tax Cuts expensing provisions his ranch ``will be able to upgrade equipment, increasing [its] efficiency without being hit by a huge tax burden.'' U.S. Metal Powders--a manufacturer in Palmerton, PA--has broken ground on a new production line that will allow the business to double the size of its workforce.

A convenience store operator in Denver has said the Working Families Tax Cuts will help him double the size of one of his stores and reopen two others, allowing him to grow job opportunities at his company by 50 percent.
One thing that business owners invariably bring up when they talk about the Working Families Tax Cuts is what it does for their employees.
The Working Families Tax Cuts was responsible for no tax on tips and overtime, which allows hard-working people to keep more of their hard- earned money.
And provisions in this legislation support employer efforts to offer childcare and help repay their employees' student loans.
I said that the Working Families Tax Cuts provides tax relief that will help small businesses and family farms and ranches for years to come.
And on that point, perhaps no policy is as significant as the death tax relief we provided in this bill.
For a lot of family businesses, especially ag families, the death tax has cast a dark shadow over their dream.
But because that doesn't matter when it comes to the death tax, many families have had to sell off all or part of their operation just to pay the tax bill when a family member dies.

Eliminating this fundamentally unfair tax has long been a priority of mine, and I am proud that the Working Families Tax Cuts permanently raised the exemption threshold on the death tax, which means that a lot more families will be protected from losing their livelihood when they lose a loved one.

A rancher in Montana said: Without the estate tax reforms . . . ranches like ours would have likely had to decide whether to sell off cattle or land just to cover the tax bill when it was time to pass it on.
These are just some of the results of the Working Families Tax Cuts, and I can't overstate how significant this bill is.

The owners of a small business in Arizona wrote in their local paper last year that if Congress had not passed the Working Families Tax Cuts, they ``would have had to raise prices and cut costs, and over time, the pressure would have only increased.'' They are not alone.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: And just in case you thought Democrat opposition was a matter of high-minded principle, since Republicans passed the Working Families Tax Cuts, a number of Democrats have tried to associate themselves with some of the tax relief in the bill despite universally opposing the legislation in Congress.
Last week, the Senate attempted to take up legislation on an issue of great importance to working families; namely, energy prices.
The legislation we tried to take up, the Ratepayer Protection Act, would have protected hard-working Americans from the increased energy costs associated with data centers.
So my Democrat colleagues may talk a good game about working families, but the truth is that hard-working Americans take a distant back seat to Democrats' political priorities.
In the spring, Senate Democrats initiated the longest partial government shutdown in history due to their unwillingness to fund immigration law enforcement or border security.
And while they eventually agreed to reopen most of the Department, they still refused to fund immigration enforcement or Border Patrol.
Clearly, democratic socialism and its philosophy of zero immigration enforcement and open borders has gained a lot more than a foothold in the Democrat Party.

Whether the subject is protecting opportunities for women and girls in sports or tax relief for hard-working Americans, Democrats have spent the past 21 months throwing up every roadblock that they can.

And I am proud that, despite the incredible amount of Democrat opposition, we still managed to accomplish a lot for the American people--from regulatory relief and border security to the Working Families Tax Cuts.
Let's just fund the government so we can continue the conversation about how we are going to fund it for the full year.
There is more work to be done, and I hope that we will get the chance to continue our work not only in this Congress but also in the next.

The official platform--the official platform of the Democratic Socialists states that their goal is to ``demilitarize police departments, disempower police unions, and redirect funding to public services as steps towards fully abolishing the police and prison system.'' Think about that: ``as steps towards fully abolishing the police and prison system''--the official platform of the Democratic Socialists of America.
If anyone thinks we can keep our communities safe while fully abolishing the police and prison system, I have some oceanfront property in South Dakota to sell them.

Swept up in their utopian fantasies, they believe that by implementing the right system--socialism--they can somehow do away with human evil and remove the need for police or prisons--or armies, for that matter.

Their platform calls for officially changing our system of government, for eliminating the Senate and replacing ``the President and Supreme Court with an executive and judiciary chosen by and subordinate to Congress.'' Those aren't tweaks around the margin; that is a full abolishment of the American system.

statements.title: Democrat Policies (Executive Session)
sentences: Mr. President, last week, I came to the floor to discuss some of the things this Republican majority has delivered over the last 2 years: permanently lowering taxes for families, a secure border.

We have worked to bring down the cost of prescription drugs and make home ownership more affordable, and we have delivered regulatory relief and tax policies to help our Nation's small businesses as well as family farms and ranches.
The Biden administration's disastrous approach to illegal immigration embraced the sanctuary policies and soft-on-crime laws for which California is the poster child.
On regulation, Democrats were determined to follow the lead of the most regulated State in the Union--especially on energy.
That is what happened with electric vehicles.
The Biden administration not only implemented its own California-style electric vehicle mandate, it also allowed California to impose a de facto EV mandate on the rest of the country.
Senators Ricketts and Husted have resolutions related to California's strict emissions standards targeting gas-powered vehicles.
Senator Schmitt has another on California's unrealistic emissions standards for cars.

Yes, as this list suggests, California will regulate just about anything that moves, ignoring the fact that these types of rules restrict consumer choice and lead to higher prices for working families.

As I mentioned, California's rush to electrification strained its power grid to the point that it faced rolling blackouts and high energy prices, and regulators had to ask residents not to charge their electric vehicles at certain hours.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: 119TH CONGRESS
statements.title: 119TH CONGRESS
sentences: And they presided over 4 straight years--4 straight years--of recordbreaking-- recordbreaking--illegal immigration.
And so in 2025, we passed the Working Families Tax Cut--sometimes known as the One Big Beautiful Bill--to prevent this massive tax hike on hard-working Americans.
We also implemented no tax on tips and no tax on overtime, substantially lowering the tax bills of millions of hard-working Americans, from Uber and Lyft drivers to hairdressers, to police officers.
And our efforts to help Americans keep more of their hard-earned money didn't stop with the Working Families Tax Cuts.

We have also spent this Congress cutting burdensome regulations that have driven up prices for hard-working Americans, from the California electric vehicle mandate, which would have forced Americans into costly electric cars, to regulations that would have driven up the cost of appliances.
As I said, in addition to reducing taxes and working to lower costs, Republicans were also committed to dealing with the Biden border crisis.
President Trump took action immediately to get the situation at our southern border under control, and the reduction in illegal immigration has been staggering.
During the last full year of the Biden border crisis, which was fiscal year 2024, there were well over 2 million illegal immigrant encounters at our southern border.
Well, we are almost done with fiscal year 2026, and do you want to know how many encounters there have been at the southern border?
And do you want to know how many of those illegal immigrants have been released into the United States?
And I don't need to tell anyone what a massive turnaround that is from the Biden administration, which presided over the release of millions of illegal immigrants into our country's interior.
The dangers of the unchecked illegal immigration that we saw under the Biden administration are manifold.

And to help prevent anything like that from happening again, the Working Families Tax Cut included substantial resources to help guarantee the security of our Nation's border from additional Border Patrol agents to security technology.
We also boosted funding for our national defense and for law enforcement.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: Republicans were committed to strengthening our economic future, ending the Biden border crisis and making America safer and stronger in the years ahead.
That was thanks to the Working Families Tax Cuts.

The American people had suffered for years through an inflation crisis caused by Democrats' reckless spending, and they were facing a massive tax hike, $2,500 for a typical family in my State if Congress had failed to act.
But the Working Families Tax Cuts made sure that tax hike never came.

We got rid of electrical vehicle mandates that were going to force Americans into pricey electric cars that they didn't want, and we have taken concrete action to drive down costs at the pharmacy counter as well.
We have seen positive news about a boost in manufacturing in our country thanks, in part, to the Working Families Tax Cuts.

The law also bolstered programs that America's farmers and ranchers depend on, and the Working Families Tax Cuts made a generational investment in rural healthcare providers in all 50 States, putting those providers on a more secure path forward so that Americans in rural areas can continue to have access to quality, affordable healthcare close to home.
I mentioned that ending the border crisis was another priority for the Senate majority, and we didn't waste any time getting to work on that either.
The first bill we passed was the Laken Riley Act, requiring that illegal immigrants who are arrested for certain crimes aren't put back on the streets.
We also passed the HALT Fentanyl Act to ensure that law enforcement has the tools it needs to go after fentanyl and fentanyl analogs that have taken too many--too many--American lives.
And then there is the border itself.

President Trump took swift action to secure the border early last year, and in the Working Families Tax Cuts, we provided the resources necessary to hire more agents, finish the border wall, and keep the border secure permanently.
Today, illegal border crossings have slowed to a trickle.
And thanks to our efforts, the resources are in place to ensure the border stays secure for the long term.
Beyond the border, we have also been focused on strengthening our military.
The Working Families Tax Cuts made a generational investment in our military readiness.
As I said, we made generational investments in border security, military readiness, and in rural healthcare.
We approved a rescissions package that cut billions in Federal spending for the first time in literally three decades.
Earlier this afternoon, we passed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, giving the President critical tools to bring peace to Ukraine.
I share his view, and we will work with him to insist and ensure that they make changes that improve the service that affects the constituents, the people that we represent and serve.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FARM BILL
statements.title: FARM BILL
sentences: That started last year with the Working Families Tax Cuts, which strengthened the farm safety net, bolstered critical farm programs, and delivered tax relief to America's agriculture producers, including relief from the unfair death tax and making the 199A deduction permanent.
It continues this year with this farm bill, which builds on the important measures in the Working Families Tax Cuts in order to give farmers and ranchers certainty into the future.
After the Working Families Tax Cuts raised reference prices last year, this farm bill makes further improvements to commodity programs as well as crop insurance--cornerstones of the farm safety net.

CRP plays a very significant role in South Dakota's economy by helping to provide habitat for pheasants, but producers in my State have been frustrated for years with how the program is managed--in particular by the fact that its restrictions on land use can be excessive.

As I said, America's farmers and ranchers are a priority for this Senate majority, and with the Working Families Tax Cuts and now this farm bill, we are making real progress on the challenges facing our producers.
That is why I introduced the CRP Improvement and Flexibility Act.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: AGOA EXTENSION ACT--Motion to Proceed
statements.title: AGOA EXTENSION ACT--Motion to Proceed
sentences: The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act cut tax rates across the board, doubled the child tax credit, and nearly doubled the standard deduction.
It put more money in hard- working Americans' pockets, money that they were able to use for their particular needs--from childcare to home repairs, to medical bills, to a family vacation.
And those same hard-working Americans were our focus last year when we passed the Working Families Tax Cuts.
Our first aim with the Working Families Tax Cuts was making the 2017 tax relief permanent, and that is exactly what we did.
We wanted to do more for working families, and so that is what we did.
Well, the Working Families Tax Cuts not only made that permanent; it increased the child tax credit even further and then indexed it to inflation so its value will never go down.
I said the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act nearly doubled the standard deduction.
Well, the Working Families Tax Cuts boosted the standard deduction even further.

That meant major new tax relief for a whole host of working Americans--waiters, delivery people, bartenders, Uber and Lyft drivers, nurses, factory workers, paramedics, police officers, and many others.

The Working Families Tax Cuts also made some significant improvements to the traditional 529 education savings plan, allowing those savings to be used for a greater variety of education-related expenses, like tutoring or home school materials and vocational and continuing education.
It is the Working Families Tax Cuts at work.
And whenever I am there, I am proud to be able to share the details of the Working Families Tax Cuts and report that Republicans are delivering for working families.
And we are going to continue to build on the Working Families Tax Cuts to expand opportunity and make life more affordable for hard- working Americans.

sentences: That bill is now known as the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act.

A party that is doing everything it can to eliminate pregnancy resource centers simply because they won't recommend abortion.
Then earlier this year, Democrats shut down the Department of Homeland Security because they didn't want to fund law enforcement.

Defunding law enforcement--once a fringe position in their party-- became the official position of the Democrat Party as they tried to completely--completely--defund Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Border Patrol.
Once again, it didn't matter to Democrats whether Americans would be less safe with open borders.
Their audience, far-left activists, wanted them to defund border security and immigration enforcement officers, so they did.

To quote the New York Times again, ``Many Americans say the [Democrat] Party does not share their priorities.'' A year and a half later, it is obvious that that is still the case: men's and women's sports, abortion up until the moment of birth, open borders, defunding law enforcement.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: National Defense Authorization Act (Executive Session)

Well, in case they were operating under a misconception, I am happy to tell them that this year's National Defense Authorization Act is not an Iran funding supplemental.
It is the annual--annual--legislation authorizing the basic needs of our military and the basic needs of our men and women in uniform, needs that exist no matter what is happening in Iran.
They voted against the reform of the Pentagon's acquisition process.
Here are the facts: Democrats can't bring themselves to authorize funding for our Nation's security, whether that is security at our border, funding for our military, or paychecks for our troops.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization (Executive Session)
statements.title: Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization (Executive Session)
sentences: Mr. President, today, we mark 4 years since the Supreme Court's Dobbs decision, the landmark Supreme Court decision overturning Roe v. Wade and returning the question of abortion to the people and their elected representatives.

Roe was, quite simply, terrible constitutional law--a fact that has been acknowledged by legal scholars across the political spectrum--and the Dobbs decision reversed this decades-old error and made it clear that Roe's supposed constitutional right to an abortion simply didn't exist.

I am proud to have fought, along with my Republican colleagues, to put Justices on the Supreme Court who focus on interpreting the law and the Constitution, instead of creating new constitutional law out of thin air, as the Justices did in Roe.
It is fitting that the Dobbs decision occurs close to our Nation's birthday, July 4, the anniversary of the adoption of the Declaration of Independence.
This is not, of course, something you will hear from my Democrat colleagues when they attempt to defend abortion.
They mention women and ``healthcare'' and ``reproductive freedom,'' as if killing an innocent person could ever, ever be something we are free to do.

And they never mention the other person in question, which is the unborn human being who was sacrificed in every abortion--probably because they know, at some level, that supporting the killing of an innocent human being is indefensible and completely incompatible with our Nation's creed.
When we talk about abortion, we are talking about the killing of a human being.
You don't even need to have seen a baby kicking her feet and sucking her thumb on an ultrasound to know that she is human because human moms and human dads have other human beings.
No, the question isn't whether the unborn baby is a human being.

I am proud to be from a State that has extended the full protection of the law to unborn human beings, that has recognized that unborn Americans are also created equal and endowed by their Creator with unalienable rights.
I am proud to have supported, sponsored, and cosponsored pro-life legislation here in Congress.
The overturning of Roe has opened the door to substantive pro-life legislation, and Republicans in Congress are going to keep up the fight for real protections for unborn Americans.
I am very proud that with the Working Families Tax Cut, Congress enacted the first pro-life law in decades.
Thanks to Republicans' landmark legislation this year, some of the Nation's largest abortion providers, including Planned Parenthood, were prohibited from receiving Federal Medicaid funding.
The Dobbs decision was a landmark decision because it opened the door for full protection of the unalienable rights of unborn Americans, but there is a lot more work to be done.

The Democrat Party fights tooth and nail to ensure that even the most commonsense measures--like measures to protect babies who survive abortions or to ensure that pregnant college students are aware that they have alternatives to abortion--do not make it through Congress.

And, currently, mail-order abortion drugs are flooding into States in defiance of the law--thanks to the Biden administration's decision to loosen restrictions on these drugs--despite the fact that they pose a danger to women, as well as obviously to the babies.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: WORKING FAMILIES TAX CUT ACT
statements.title: WORKING FAMILIES TAX CUT ACT
sentences: Mr. President, I spoke on the floor yesterday about the landmark bill Republicans passed last year, the Working Families Tax Cut bill, and I talked about how this bill fits into Republicans' efforts to turn things around in our country, turn things around by putting more money in Americans' pockets, helping small businesses grow, strengthening the agriculture sector, and giving a lifeline to rural healthcare.

Any one of those things alone would have been a significant achievement, but the Working Families Tax Cut addressed all of them, all of them and more, much more, and this morning I want to talk about how this bill helps to make America more secure.
Images of the chaos at the southern border during the Biden administration come to mind, so does the state of our military readiness.
As part of the Working Families Tax Cut, Republicans made a generational investment in America's military.
As I mentioned, we also needed to address border security.

When President Trump took office, he wasted no time implementing policies that restored order at America's southern border and put criminal illegal immigrants living in our country on notice, and we saw the results.
Border agents weren't being stretched so thin anymore and could spend more time stopping cartels and other criminals.
That is how things should be at the border, and Republicans are making sure that it stays that way.
As part of the Working Families Tax Cut, we made a generational investment in border security.
We provided the resources necessary to finish the border wall and deploy additional barriers and technology to secure the border.

Thanks to President Trump and the Working Families Tax Cut, as of the end of last month, apprehensions at the southern border are more than 90 percent lower than they were under the Biden administration.

Border Patrol is seeing a few hundred border crossings on a typical day compared to as many as 10,000 in a single day, at times, under President Biden, and not a single illegal immigrant has been released from the border in more than a year.
The American people support border security, and keeping America safe should be something that cuts across party lines.
Unfortunately, our Democratic colleagues have repeatedly demonstrated zero interest in border security, and they consistently reaffirm their belief in open borders.
First, there was their complicit silence as the Biden administration opened our borders to a flood of illegal immigrants.
Then, every Democrat opposed our border security measures in the Working Families Tax Cut.
And then this year--this year--Democrats took their radical open border beliefs to a new level and tried to defund Border Patrol and ICE.

Fortunately, Democrats' radical proposal did not carry the day, and Republicans were, once again, able to fund border security and immigration enforcement, unfortunately, without Democrats' assistance.
The Working Families Tax Cut is a big step toward a more secure America.
It invests in safer streets with funding for State and local law enforcement, safer skies by supporting air traffic control modernization, a secure border, and a strong military.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: Madam President, we are approaching 1 year since the Working Families Tax Cut became law.

For nearly a year now, the American people have been seeing the benefits of this bill, from a more secure border to a stronger military, larger paychecks and bigger refunds, support for farmers and ranchers, and a lifeline for struggling rural healthcare providers.
For the past year, the story of the Working Families Tax Cut has been unfolding across the country in different ways.
Thanks to the Working Families Tax Cut, 97 percent of Americans that filed this year got a tax cut.
And 29 million workers--from nurses to police officers and factory workers--took advantage of the new overtime deduction.

The Working Families Tax Cut also delivered meaningful pro-growth tax reforms for Americans' small businesses, farms, and ranches, enabling them to invest more in their operations and in their employees.
One agricultural co-op in my State estimates the impact of that one provision helped its co-op members reinvest more than $100 million into our local economy in the last 10 years.

In fact, our former colleague, a neighbor to the north in North Dakota, former Democrat Senator Heidi Heitkamp has said: For many producers and ag-related businesses, this is more than a tax break; this is a real opportunity to reinvest, innovate, and stay competitive.

And although I haven't mentioned the higher estate tax threshold that protects a lot more family farms and ranchers from the death tax, not to mention the costly estate planning that comes with that unfair tax, but this bill went further than tax relief; it strengthened critical programs that producers depend upon.

We still have more work to do to strengthen the ag sector, but the Working Families Tax Cut delivered meaningful relief to farmers after a challenging few years, defined by higher input costs, higher interest rates, and national disasters--all while many farm programs were inadequate to meet the circumstances that farmers were living in.
So last year in the Working Families Tax Cut, Republicans did something to address the rural healthcare crisis.
Later today, we will pass a housing affordability bill.

The Agriculture Committee is continuing to work on a farm bill and additional agricultural relief, and we continue important legislative efforts on issues from cryptocurrency to artificial intelligence, to reining in waste, fraud, and abuse in the Federal Government.
One year ago, Republicans delivered major wins for the American people in the Working Families Tax Cut, and we are working every day to build on that success and to deliver again and again.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: Limited housing supply and burdensome regulations have contributed to higher prices, and many Americans are simply being priced out of the housing market.

And because Federal regulations are only one layer of the costs and burdens placed on new home construction, this bill also encourages local governments to reform zoning laws to encourage home construction.

I am grateful for the work of Senators Rounds and Ricketts to support housing in rural areas, for Senators Moreno and Hagerty's contributions to the financial institutions component of this bill, and for Senators Kennedy and Crapo's efforts to support work at the local level to build more housing.
Last year, Republicans passed the Working Families Tax Cut, another landmark bill which cut taxes for lower and middle-income Americans.

Plus, the Working Families Tax Cut provisions like immediate, 100 percent expensing for investments are also contributing to addressing housing shortages by making it easier for builders to--well--build.
Our legislation gave a boost to affordable housing construction as well.
A recent poll shows that the overwhelming majority of Americans see housing affordability as a major issue, and they want to see Congress address it.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: National Defense Authorization Act of 2027 (Executive Session)
statements.title: National Defense Authorization Act of 2027 (Executive Session)
sentences: Mr. President, last week, a U.S. Army Apache helicopter went down off the coast of Iran.
From the battlefields of Ukraine to the conflict with Iran, drones and other unmanned systems have become the weapon of choice.
This year's bill builds on the significant reforms to defense acquisition we enacted in last year's NDAA in a number of ways.
It also supports a number of quality-of-life improvements, including investments in education, healthcare, and childcare for servicemembers and their families.
We need to be the leader in the capabilities that will define the future--capabilities that will keep Americans safe by making our enemies think twice before crossing us.
Try as we might, we simply don't know what is coming over the horizon, and we will eventually pay the price for failing to invest in a strong national defense today.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SENATE DEMOCRATS
statements.title: SENATE DEMOCRATS

And eventually, they just walked away completely and refused to provide even a dollar of funding for Border Patrol or ICE.

Democrats shut down the government twice to try to improve their chances in November, not to help hard-working Americans, not to get reforms at ICE and Border Patrol--no; to improve their chances in November.
So were a lot of civilian government employees like the Capitol Police officers who stand on guard for us around this building.
I wonder if they would try to undo the tax relief Republicans passed for working families which every single Democrat voted against.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: NOMINATION OF WALTER CLAYTON
statements.title: NOMINATION OF WALTER CLAYTON

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: NATIONAL SECURITY
statements.title: NATIONAL SECURITY
sentences: Mr. President, last week, Senate Republicans passed legislation to fund Border Patrol and Immigration and Customs Enforcement for the next 3 years.
Republicans are deeply committed to ensuring a safe country and safe communities, and border security and immigration enforcement are key parts of that.
No country--no country--can be secure if bad actors can make their way freely across the borders or criminal illegal immigrants are able to operate freely within our neighborhoods.
And then there is border security and immigration enforcement.
Democrats absolutely refused to provide so much as a dollar--a dollar-- to fund the agents who provide security at our Nation's borders and remove criminal illegal immigrants from America's streets.
If Democrats had their way, there would be zero--zero--physical presence at our Nation's borders and zero agents to remove criminal illegal immigrants who do make their way into our country.
They shut down the Federal Government twice and refused to fund border security and immigration enforcement because they couldn't take yes for an answer.

And if our economy suffers, if our national security suffers because of Democrats' decision to shut down the government or refusal to fund border security, well, Democrats are apparently just fine with that.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: THEODORE ROOSEVELT NATIONAL PARK WILD HORSES PROTECTION ACT
statements.title: THEODORE ROOSEVELT NATIONAL PARK WILD HORSES PROTECTION ACT
sentences: More recently, Border Patrol and Immigration and Customs Enforcement, two Agencies that are critical to keeping this country safe--they don't want to provide a single dollar--zero--zero dollars for ICE and CBP, making this country less safe.

Something was negotiated in a bipartisan way to get a bill on the floor that we could use to extend this program and continue to keep Americans safe.
This is a program that works, and it works effectively to keep Americans safe.

So what I am going to do is suggest, because this acting temporary person doesn't even get into the acting temporary position until a week from tomorrow, June 19, I am going to suggest that we do at least a 1- week extension to keep the lights on at this Agency, at a time when we are hosting the World Cup.

So, again, I will simply say this is, on its face, an irresponsible position that makes America and Americans less safe.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: Working Families Tax Cut Act (Executive Session)
statements.title: Working Families Tax Cut Act (Executive Session)
sentences: Mr. President, it has been almost a year since Republicans passed the Working Families Tax Cut, 1 year since Republicans delivered permanent tax relief to the American people and put more money in their pockets.

The New York Times interviewed three dozen Americans, who reported that ``many of the taxpayers said they had received their largest refund in years,'' allowing them to pay down debt, save more, or cover the cost of a vacation or a new bed.
Last week, we got yet more news that shows that the Working Families Tax Cut is working.
Thanks to the Working Families Tax Cut, 97 percent of taxpayers got a tax cut this year, collectively saving about $82 billion on their tax bills.
And who was it--who was it--that benefited from the Working Families Tax Cut?
It is in the name: working families.
I will get into each of those specifics here in just a minute, but I think it is important to point out that the beneficiaries of the Working Families Tax Cut were working families.
And that is who Republicans were thinking about when we wrote the Working Families Tax Cut, and as the numbers show, that is who is benefiting.
I have said that the Working Families Tax Cut is about putting more money in hard-working Americans' pockets, and that is exactly what this bill did.

It let working Americans keep more of their hard-earned money--money that they would have had to send to the IRS if not for the Working Families Tax Cut and that they can now spend, invest, and save as they see fit.
The Working Families Tax Cut delivered real taxing savings to the American people through a number of tax relief policies.

A New York Times story in April on this year's larger tax refunds highlighted Nicole Mendoza, a 68-year-old Georgian who ``works a couple of shifts a week at a Cracker Barrel in Canton, Ga., to supplement her Social Security income and savings.
This year, millions of hard-working Americans like Ms. Mendoza were eligible for additional tax relief thanks to the Working Families Tax Cut.
That is pretty stunning, if you think about it, if you talk about actually working families out there, people who are trying to make ends meet.
That is the Working Families Tax Cut in action.
The Working Families Tax Cut is delivering for working Americans.
As they have every time that Republicans have lowered taxes for working people, Democrats have resurrected their dusty, old talking points about tax cuts for the rich.
I can't count the number of times that I have heard a Democrat Senator say this bill was just about tax cuts for billionaires.
Does this look like a billionaire tax cut to you?

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FOREIGN INTELLIGENCE SURVEILLANCE ACT
statements.title: FOREIGN INTELLIGENCE SURVEILLANCE ACT

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: IMMIGRATION
statements.title: IMMIGRATION
sentences: Mr. President, sometimes, I have to wonder if Democrats remember the last election and how 4 years of recordbreaking illegal immigration on President Biden's watch helped hand the House, the Senate, and the White House to Republicans, because to watch the Democrat Party right now, you would think that 2024 never happened.
Democrats not only haven't rejected the open borders philosophy of the Biden administration; they have doubled down.
At least we had the Border Patrol and Immigration and Customs Enforcement under President Biden.
Democrats voted to defund--to defund--the agents who stand guard on our Nation's borders and help prevent dangerous individuals from entering our country.
They voted to defund the agents who remove criminal illegal immigrants who do make their way into the United States.
And when I say ``defund,'' I mean defund.
But Democrats weren't interested, presumably because they somehow thought that ``defund law enforcement'' and ``abolish border security'' would play well for them in November.
Of course, I am pretty sure most Americans don't think we should eliminate security at our Nation's borders or open the floodgates for unchecked illegal immigration.

But that hasn't stopped Democrats from embracing ``defund the police 2.0.'' I am happy to report that, as of Friday, Democrats' crusade to defund border security and law enforcement is well on its way to failure--for now--for now, at any rate.
Senate Republicans passed legislation to fund Border Patrol and Immigration and Customs Enforcement for the next 3 years to ensure that Democrats can't try defunding these Agencies again this fall.

But it is deeply disturbing that we are in this position, that we are having to use the reconciliation process just to get normal appropriations passed for border security and immigration enforcement.

And then there is our subject today, ``defund the police 2.0''--the Democrats' resolute refusal to spend a single dollar protecting our Nation's borders or deporting criminals here in our country illegally.

On our watch, there will be agents at our borders to prevent terrorists, traffickers, and other dangerous individuals from making their way into our country, and there will be agents to take criminal illegal immigrants off of America's streets.
As long as Republicans are in charge, we will be focused on both the economic challenges facing our country and on securing peace and safety for hard-working Americans.

statements.title: RECOGNITION OF THE MAJORITY LEADER

Because Democrats have refused to fund border security or immigration law enforcement.
We are here today only--only--because Democrats refuse to appropriate a single dollar for our border and immigration law enforcement.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: TRUMP ACCOUNTS
statements.title: TRUMP ACCOUNTS
sentences: These are new tax-advantaged investment accounts for children created by the Republicans' Working Families Tax Cut.
Trump Accounts, as I said, were created as part of the Republicans' Working Families Tax Cut law.
We call it the Working Families Tax Cut for a reason--because that is whom we were focused on with this legislation.
All of these measures were designed to help everyday Americans and to make life a little easier for working families and help put their dreams within reach.

And she has said of the Trump Accounts: This program will benefit everyone, decreasing the gap for future prosperity between children who traditionally aren't born with a full bank account and children who are. ``[d]ecreasing the gap for future prosperity between children who traditionally aren't born with a full bank account and children who are.'' Increasing opportunity, opening new paths to prosperity, ensuring that working families can keep more of their hard-earned money, that is Republicans' mission, and the goal of the Working Families Tax Cut.
I am proud that working families are benefiting, and I look forward to seeing the opportunities that will be unlocked next month when Trump Accounts kick off.
Mr. President, as of tomorrow, we will be one month away from the opening date for Trump Accounts.

statements.title: C-SPAN2
sentences: As I mentioned, I met with the mayor of Webster Mike Grosek, and I dropped by a few local businesses that are benefiting from the permanent tax relief Republicans delivered in the Working Families Tax Cut.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY
statements.title: DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY
sentences: Supporting the men and women who do this important work--funding law enforcement--isn't optional either.

Incredibly, Democrats have refused to provide a single penny for border security and immigration law enforcement for fiscal year 2026--that is zero dollars for a physical presence at our Nation's border; zero dollars to deport criminals who have made their way into our country illegally.
If Democrats had their way, illegal immigrants would be allowed to flood across our Nation's southern border entirely unchecked.
After all, it is hardly the first time Democrats have demonstrated that border security and immigration enforcement are at the very bottom of their priority list.
For decades now, Democrat-led cities and States have implemented sanctuary policies that prevent local law enforcement from cooperating with Federal immigration authorities.
Then there was the crisis at the southern border.
There were 4--4-- straight years of recordbreaking illegal immigration at our southern border under Democrats and President Biden.
The New York Times reported: After Mr. Biden became president, migrant encounters at the southern border quickly doubled, then kept rising.
New arrivals overwhelmed border stations, then border towns, and eventually major cities like New York and Denver.
Illegal crossings have plummeted to a trickle, and as of the end of April, not a single illegal immigrant has been released at the border and into our country for an entire year.
But Democrats are apparently determined to bring back unchecked illegal immigration.
To do that, they are embracing the far-left ideologies of ``defund law enforcement'' and ``abolish ICE.'' These were once considered fringe positions among Democrats.
The junior Senator from California said in January: I'm not giving ICE or Border Patrol another dime.
The junior Senator from Massachusetts told a crowd in February: We know that we must defund and abolish ICE.
Needless to say, as long as Republicans are in charge, we are not going to let Democrats defund border security and immigration law enforcement.
I don't know who Democrats think benefits from blocking funding for Border Patrol and ICE.
The American people certainly don't benefit from there being no law enforcement at the border.
Democrats' position puts illegal immigrants in danger as well.
Border Patrol agents are the ones pulling illegal immigrants out of the Rio Grande and rescuing dehydrated migrants in the desert.
If Democrats' position helps anyone, it helps the cartels, the coyotes, and other criminals who prefer to act without risk of detection and apprehension.

Democrats haven't exactly demonstrated an eagerness to come to the floor and defend open borders, and I strongly suspect that is because at some level, they know their position is completely indefensible.
President Trump and Republicans have cleaned up Democrats' mess at the border.
We have secured the southern border and put criminals on notice that they will no longer be living freely in our country.
And we plan to keep it that way.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: RECONCILIATION
statements.title: RECONCILIATION
sentences: Everyone remembers the Democrat Party's flirtation with ``defund the police'' a few years ago.
But when it rapidly became apparent that we actually need the police, Democrats seemed to rein things in.
In today's Democrat Party, ``defund the police'' is back and more strongly than ever.

The reason we are here today, I would say the sole--sole--reason we are here today is because we are considering this reconciliation bill because Democrats refuse to fund law enforcement at the Department of Homeland Security.
They refuse to fund Border Patrol, and they refuse to fund Immigrations and Customs Enforcement--at all.

They wouldn't agree to provide a single dollar for either of these Agencies--not a single dollar for a physical presence at our border, not a single dollar to take criminal illegal aliens off of our streets.

The public record provides ample evidence of the fact that among those who try to make their way illegally across the border, there are bad actors whose presence in this country would endanger Americans.

Democrats don't want there to be a single individual at the border to stop those individuals from entering our country, and they don't want there to be a single individual to enforce immigration law in this country.
The various women who were murdered by illegal immigrants who entered the country under the open borders Biden administration--what about them?

If this were about making reforms to the way ICE or Border Patrol does business, then Democrats would have accepted the robust package of legislative reforms they were offered by the White House or engaged in serious negotiations to tweak the package, but they didn't.
Of course, I am not sure what political constituency they were appealing to because I don't think mainstream Americans believe in, for example, completely defunding our Nation's Border Patrol.

In recent days, perhaps realizing just how extreme ``defund the police'' could seem to mainstream American, the Democrat leader has attempted to obfuscate what is happening here by suggesting that Republicans' consideration of this bill somehow means that Republicans are not concerned with the challenges facing ordinary Americans.

From legislation to drive down the cost of prescription drugs at the pharmacy counter to our signature Working Families Tax Cut, which permanently cut American taxes and put more money in workers' pockets, Republicans have been focused--focused like a laser--on making life easier for hard-working Americans.

As long as we are in charge, there will be agents at our borders to prevent terrorists, traffickers, and other dangerous individuals from making their way into our country, and there will be agents to take criminal illegal immigrants off of America's streets.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: GOVERNMENT FUNDING
statements.title: GOVERNMENT FUNDING
sentences: A bill, I might add, that included bipartisan reforms and money for additional body cameras for immigration enforcement.
And apparently they decided that defunding law enforcement would be a winner for them because that is what we are talking about here.
Democrats voted to defund border security.
They voted to defund immigration enforcement--not reform, defund, and defund completely.

A few weeks ago on the floor, the Democrat leader said that ICE and Border Patrol are two agencies that ``nobody respects in this country.'' Nobody respects Border Patrol and ICE; those are the Democrat leader's words.
Apparently, the fact that there are men and women risking their lives against drug cartels and gang members doesn't merit respect from Democrats.
For years now, Democrat-led cities and States have implemented sanctuary policies to prevent their law enforcement agencies from cooperating with immigration authorities.
The murder of Laken Riley is just one example.
Then, under President Biden, Democrats' embrace of open border policies reached its zenith.
The Biden administration clearly did not believe in enforcing our immigration laws, and the result was year upon year of recordbreaking illegal immigration.
As even the New York Times has reported: After Mr. Biden became president, migrant encounters at the southern border quickly doubled, then kept rising.
New arrivals overwhelmed border stations, then border towns, and eventually major cities like New York and Denver.
Still Democrats embrace open borders.
And make no mistake, that is exactly what Democrats are embracing when they opt for giving no funding--zero funding--to Border Patrol and ICE.
They are suggesting that we don't have law enforcement officers taking criminal illegal immigrants off of our streets.

And I really have to wonder who they are doing this for because letting illegal immigrants enter our country unchecked and allowing criminal illegal immigrants to roam free is certainly not putting the American people first.
They would rather have applause from the far-left ``defund the police'' crowd than keep the American people safe.
We are going to ensure our immigration laws are enforced and criminal illegal aliens are not allowed to live freely in our country.
And if Democrats want to play partisan games and vote against border security, well, they are free to do that.
But Republicans are going to do our jobs and ensure that law enforcement can do theirs.
And we will be moving forward with the final steps of that process shortly.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: Trump Administration (Executive Session)
statements.title: Trump Administration (Executive Session)
sentences: We lifted costly Biden-era regulations, from rules that would have driven up the cost of household appliances to rules that would have forced Americans into expensive electric vehicles.
At the start of this year, we took action to drive down the cost of prescription drugs at the pharmacy counter.

Lifting costly regulations and taking action to lower the cost of prescriptions and housing are significant actions, but what I consider to be the most consequential action not just of this majority but of my entire time in the Senate is the Working Families Tax Cut.
That was the centerpiece of this bill, and a whole lot of Americans saw that last month when they filed their tax returns and saw a significantly higher refund.
The Working Families Tax Cut lets hard-working people keep more of their hard-earned money.

And a lot of family business owners, farmers, and ranchers breathe a sigh of relief when this bill passed because it protects them from a potentially devastating death tax bill, not to mention the costly estate planning expenses that come along with this tax.
In the Working Families Tax Cut, we made lasting reforms to strengthen the farm safety net.

The Working Families Tax Cut included a number of reforms to focus Federal dollars on those most in need, guard against the abuse of taxpayer funds, and hold States accountable for the Federal funding they receive.
New measures in the law prevent noncitizens from receiving Federal healthcare and nutrition benefits and refocus those programs on serving American citizens.

The law requires States to be good stewards of Federal programs like Medicaid and nutrition assistance, and it takes aim at duplicative enrollment in Federal healthcare programs, which CMS estimates costs taxpayers as much as $14 billion per year.
The Working Families Tax Cut prevented Americans' tax dollars from funding big abortion providers for 1 year.

Last summer, Republicans passed a rescissions package that targeted funding that had gone to some egregious misuses of taxpayer dollars, like a pride parade in Lesotho and promoting vegan food in Zambia.
Their refusal to provide even a dollar for the Border Patrol in this year's DHS funding bill is ample evidence of that.
Republicans most certainly believe in border security.
In fact, addressing the dangerous situation at our southern border was one of our top priorities when we took over last year.
The first bill we passed was the Laken Riley Act to ensure that illegal immigrants who committed certain crimes are not allowed back on our streets.
We passed the HALT Fentanyl Act to give law enforcement the tools it needs to go after this deadly poison, much of which flows across our southern border.
The Working Families Tax Cut made a generational investment in border security, and we are seeing the results of that investment and the Trump administration's actions at the border.
Encounters at our southern border have dropped dramatically.

As soon as this week, we will take up a bill to fully fund Border Patrol and Immigration and Customs Enforcement for the remainder of the Trump administration and ensure the Democrats cannot put our Nation's security in jeopardy by defunding law enforcement.
They blocked Senator Tuberville's Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act, which would have simply prevented biological men from competing in women's sports.

They blocked Senator Lankford's Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act, which would have required that babies who survive abortion are given the same level of care as babies born at the same gestational age.
Then, just recently, Democrats blocked the SAVE America Act.

Republicans gave Democrats opportunities to support the whole bill, and we had standalone votes on some of the individual and very commonsense components of the bill: requiring proof of citizenship to register to vote, requiring a photo ID to vote, protecting children from gender transition surgeries, keeping biological men out of women's sports.

Last week, the Banking Committee advanced the CLARITY Act--a market structure bill for cryptocurrencies that builds on the GENIUS Act that became law last year and which was the first- ever crypto bill passed into law.
I expect the Senate will also take action on an artificial intelligence bill this year that builds on the AI framework the White House has put out.
The House has passed a bill to allow year-round E15, and we will be having discussions on how to accomplish that goal in the Senate in the near future.
Democrats are on the record against all of it, and we will be sure the American people know that Democrats are blocking commonsense policies that have broad support from the American people.
In the near term, we will also need to extend FISA and ensure that this critical national security program does not go dark.

We will soon begin work on the fiscal year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act, which will continue Republicans' efforts to modernize America's military, and, of course, we will continue to prioritize efforts to make life easier for hard-working Americans.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: NATIONAL POLICE WEEK
statements.title: NATIONAL POLICE WEEK
sentences: Mr. President, last month, a Sioux Falls, SD, police officer responded to a report of a weapons violation.

Here in DC last month, law enforcement officers on duty at the White House Correspondents' Dinner responded when an individual darted through a security checkpoint with the intent of assassinating the President and members of his administration.
The job of a law enforcement officer is an unpredictable one.
Police officers, law enforcement officers, don't have that same assurance.
The job of a police officer is unpredictable.

Some days might be very quiet--helping a stranded motorist, writing a speeding ticket, chatting with kids about police work at a school function--but other days--other days--a police officer might respond to a call and be confronted with a gunman.
Law enforcement officers never know what kind of day it will be.
Yet, every day, men and women across this country embrace their jobs in law enforcement.
This week, we observe National Police Week to honor the service and sacrifice of our Nation's law enforcement officers.
Tomorrow, we observe National Peace Officers Memorial Day--a day to remember the men and women of law enforcement who have given their lives in the line of duty.

This year's Police Week resolution notes that in 2025, more than 200 officers were killed in the line of duty--200 men and women who left their homes in the morning and failed to return to it at the end of the day.
As we honor the service and sacrifice of our Nation's law enforcement officers, we also need to honor their families because their families also serve.
And every year, for some law enforcement families, that fear comes true, and this week and every week, we should remember them.

This Police Week, I want to say a special thank-you to South Dakota law enforcement officers--police officers, sheriff's deputies, State troopers, Tribal police, and the Federal officers who serve our State.
I also want to thank the officers of the Capitol Police, who stand guard in this building every hour of every day.
To all of our Nation's law enforcement officers, today and every day, thank you.
Of course, all of life has uncertainty, but when most of us depart our houses every day, we can be pretty certain that we will return that evening the same way we left that morning--in safety.

statements.title: Small Businesses (Executive Session)
sentences: That is why they were a key focus of the tax relief we delivered in the Working Families Tax Cuts last year.

For those who work in hospitality and tourism, summer means more customers and more money, and the Working Families Tax Cuts ensures that more of the money they earn stays in their pockets.
Democrats may try to claim the Working Families Tax Cuts was about billionaires, but the American people know the truth.

Farmers, ranchers, and small business owners know it is helping them free up money to meet their expenses and invest in their operations and in their employees, and hard-working Americans can see that the Working Families Tax Cuts lets them keep more of their hard-earned money.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY
statements.title: DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY
sentences: Mr. President, we have a lot to do over the next 2 weeks: confirm Kevin Warsh to the Federal Reserve, approve a nominations package, and fund law enforcement at the Department of Homeland Security.
We should have been able to have funded border security and immigration enforcement officers as part of the final Homeland Security funding agreement, but my Democrat colleagues refused.
In fact, the Democrat leader said today that Democrats will fight legislation to fund law enforcement at DHS with ``every tool we have.'' It is difficult to believe that we are here again.
We all remember the ``defund the police'' movement embraced by the left and members of the Democrat Party.

We also remember how cities who moved to defund the police backtracked in pretty short order because it turns out, as even some leftists came to realize, we need police officers; we need law enforcement.
We need men and women who courageously dedicate their lives to law enforcement.
I can scarcely think of anything more obvious, but, apparently, the need for law enforcement is not obvious to my Democrat colleagues because they are right back to a ``defund the police'' position.

This time, it is defunding law enforcement at the Department of Homeland Security, specifically Border Patrol and Immigration and Customs Enforcement, the men and women--the men and women--who patrol our borders and take dangerous criminal illegal immigrants off of our streets.
Mr. President, when I say defunding law enforcement and DHS, I don't mean reducing the budget.
They refused to provide a single dollar for the men and women who take dangerous criminal illegal aliens off of our street.
My Democrat colleagues, apparently, believe there should be no physical presence at our borders and no law enforcement officers to deport dangerous criminals who have entered our country illegally.
We had 4 years of chaos at the southern border under President Biden, but at least we had the Border Patrol, overstretched as it was.
Now Democrats, apparently, believe in removing all law enforcement officers from our Nation's borders.

I shouldn't need to state the obvious here: that we need border security and immigration enforcement officers to protect our Nation, just as we need police officers and FBI agents and Secret Service agents and all of the law enforcement officers who serve our communities.

Democrats might like to pretend otherwise, but there are dangerous individuals who would like to make their way illegally across our border--drug traffickers, human traffickers, other criminals, terrorists.

And the men and women of the Border Patrol and Immigration and Customs Enforcement are the men and women who stand between us and these dangerous individuals, who turn them back at our borders and take them out of our communities, if they do manage to make their way into our country.
These are the men and women my Democrat colleagues want to defund-- not reform.
They want to defund and defund completely--zero--zero agents at our border, zero agents to deport criminals here in the United States illegally.
It is Police Week this week, a week to honor our Nation's law enforcement officers and remember those who made the ultimate sacrifice while protecting our communities.
Perhaps--perhaps--it will remind my Democrat colleagues of just how much we rely on law enforcement and just how much we need all--all--of our Nation's law enforcement officers. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY
statements.title: DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY
sentences: In fact, they don't really seem to care whether some of our laws, particularly laws dealing with border security and illegal immigration, get enforced at all.
And they are even trying to defund the very Agencies that enforce those laws.
That is right: no funding for Immigration and Customs Enforcement; no funding for Border Patrol.
Democrats apparently think it is reasonable to have nobody patrolling the southern border.
They think it is reasonable to let criminal illegal immigrants continue living freely in our country.
While our Democrat colleagues try to appeal to the ``defund the police'' crowd, Republicans are doing our job.
Last week, Senate Republicans moved forward to begin a process that will allow us to fund Border Patrol and Immigration and Customs Enforcement without-- without--Democrats.
And in order to prevent Democrats from trying to defund law enforcement again in September, we are going to fund these Agencies for the next 3 years.
We are going to give these law enforcement officers certainty that they won't be used as political pawns by Democrats and that they will be able to do the job they were hired to do.
Protecting our borders and deporting criminal illegal aliens are essential components of our country's security.
Last week, the Democrat leader said that Border Patrol and ICE are two Agencies that ``nobody respects in this country.'' ``Nobody respects Border Patrol and ICE.'' That is what he said.
The Biden administration clearly did not believe in enforcing immigration laws, and the result was 4 years of recordbreaking illegal immigration under President Biden's watch.

And long before the Biden border crisis, Democrat-led cities and States were implementing sanctuary city policies that prevented their law enforcement agencies from working with Federal law enforcement to get criminal illegal immigrants off our streets.
Laken Riley is just one example.

After being arrested in New York City, he was released before Immigration and Customs Enforcement could issue a detainer, a request that police hold an individual so that he could be taken into immigration custody.
And so this individual, here in the United States illegally--and subsequently involved in two crimes--was free on the University of Georgia campus when Laken Riley went running in February of 2024.

A man, who had illegally entered our country and then committed not one but two crimes in our country, should not have been free on our streets, but he was because of open border and sanctuary policies implemented by Democrats.
Today, Democrats are advocating for defunding border security and immigration enforcement.
They are advocating for a return to the policies that led to tragedies like the murder of Laken Riley, policies that led to a crisis at the southern border and made America and Americans less safe.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY
statements.title: DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY
sentences: Mr. President, we need law enforcement.
We need the police officers who patrol our streets, the first to respond when someone is in danger or needs help.
We need sheriffs' offices and transit police and ATF agents, and, yes, we need the Federal law enforcement officers who patrol our borders and take dangerous illegal aliens off of our streets.
Ask most Americans, and I think you would find they say: Of course--of course--we need law enforcement.
The ``defund the police'' movement and ``abolish ICE'' movements were both embraced by Members of the Democrat Party, and now Democrats are at it again.
The Department of Homeland Security has been shut down because Democrats decided they don't want to fund border security or immigration enforcement.
They refuse to fund the Border Patrol.
They refuse to fund Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
They are refusing to fund any physical presence at our borders or any agents to take dangerous criminal illegal aliens off of our streets.

Not only that, the Democrat leader made it very clear that his party doesn't ever--he doesn't even, I should say, respect the work these law enforcement agents are doing. ``Nobody in this country respects ICE and Border Patrol,'' the Democrat leader said on the floor last week.

And when asked to clarify his comments to say whether he really thinks nobody respects agents who put their lives on the line to, for example, stop dangerous individuals from crossing the border, the Democrat leader declined to answer.
Declining to fund these key law enforcement Agencies is a pretty good clue that Democrats don't respect the sacrifices these agents make to protect our country.
Why do we need law enforcement officers?
Border Patrol agents stop them.
And when dangerous individuals do make their way into our country, Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents work to take these dangerous individuals off of our streets.
They may not like the fact that we need border security and immigration enforcement.
But the fact remains that Border Patrol and Immigration and Customs Enforcement are two Agencies that play a key role in our safety.

And the enormity of what Democrats have opted for cannot be overstated: no agents--zero agents--at the border; no one--no one--to stop dangerous individuals from making their way into our country; and no one--no one--to catch and deport these dangerous individuals if they do make it in.
As long as we are in charge, we are going to do everything we can to protect our borders and keep dangerous criminal illegal aliens off of our streets.

And that is why, after weeks and weeks of attempting to negotiate a funding agreement with Democrats before they ultimately walked away, we are now set to consider a reconciliation bill to fund border security and immigration enforcement for the next 3 years.
